docs.text: I’ve been to Berlin, Zurich, and Rome on this trip, and although I spent the least time there, I’ll say this for Zurich: They’ve got some of the best tap water I’ve ever had. (NYC level, just short of Detroit’s pristine tap from the bottom of Lake Huron)

No, I've never lived with one. I could have used one at the house I was making videos in (much of Illinois has bonkers hard water, including out there) but I just dealt with it. And now that I'm back on Chicago municipal water from Lake Michigan, it's not terribly hard.
I really like the clean fresh water of Lake Michigan.
Somebody should bring an energy drink to the park ranger at the lake superior maritime visitor center
Last night at dinner, our server kept refilling my iced tea and I guess I was thirsty because in 2.5 hours I think I drank the equivalent of Lake Erie
I live right next to the Great Lakes Our water tastes like water (Sorry for the brag TwT)
My Lake Michigan tap water stickers are better than yours.

Well, since it seems that we are still in the water topic circle i would say i drank any type of water. Preferably those that fall under the drinkable type. Although, i am quite interested on trying out the waters of the Great Lakes. So many colours bound to be different tastes.

All-time best tap water cities I’ve lived in: 1. Detroit. Lake Huron water, chilly, clean, and perfect
2. New York City. Cool, potent, electric
3. Philadelphia. Wildly variable. Best is just fine, worst needs to be left out overnight to dissolve.
4. Chicago. Lake Michigan can’t hang
5. Lansing. No
How I feel knowing that my glass of Hoppes is good for me as I sip on the beaches of Lake Huron
Tap water drawn from Lake Superior tastes amazing. That water really goes through a lot before it reaches my intake pipe in the Niagara River, and you can taste it.

Gross and wrong. Not everyone likes the taste of subway runoff and lead. There’s a midwestern latitude sweet spot of superior tap water that runs across I-70 of KC, STL, Indy, Cincy that avoids both the Chicago-y Great Lakes water hardness and southeastern funk.
Given the reliance on Great Lakes for water... I'd say we're all cooked.

(Of cities I’ve lived in, the best tap water is Detroit’s, fresh from Lake Huron. NYC is number two. Philadelphia badly needs a filter. Chicago underperforms for a Great Lakes city. Bay Area water is usually not good. East Lansing, MI is last)

Moderately interesting logistics fact of the day: my folks and I strongly prefer the taste of the tap water we’ve had in Hinsdale and Westmont to that of Pentwater. It turns out that despite being right on the Lake, Pentwater uses well water, while both IL towns get Lake Michigan water via the DWC.
i will admit i barely did my googles on this one, but lake michigans water seems so clean. i know lake tahoe is the cleanest lake in the u.s. but i wonder where lake michigan falls. 🤔
My kitchen tap water from out of Lake Michigan is the best water ever.
Used to dip a cup into Lake Huron off the side of the sailboat and drink it all the time, as a kid.
As someone who cooks allll the time, if I couldn't cook with my tap water I'd go nuts, I'd have to get so many water jugs 😖😵‍💫, but I suppose I'm spoiled living near the Great lakes all my life
That doesn’t mean you need to drink the volume of Lake Superior every day though 😘
I'm drinking a tall glass of Lake Superior right now.
At least if you're stranded on Lake Superior you can drink it!

The only water I would, and have drunk directly from the source is from Lake Superior, from the north end of the Keweenaw Peninsula. It was not without issue, however. While I didn't develop any intestinal trouble, I was thrown against the rocky beach trying to collect it, and nearly broke my arm.

I'm JUST old enough to remember still drinking well water. It tastes kind of metallic and heavy, but otherwise it's, well...water (ha ha!). Still, my town, through my dad's efforts as mayor, got hooked up with Lake Michigan water, which improved the quality.

I am putting my bets on the water. Lake Michigan water has the perfect alkalinity for pizza dough and craft beer, believe it or not. Anywhere I’ve lived in IL has been on lake water. Maybe there is just some mineral composition of DC water that I personally just don’t like lol

Yeah, I'm sure there is some getting used to it involved. I think lake Michigan water is particularly good overall for flavour. Well water can get a bit weird. Idk. Generally I've had pretty awesome water luck though. I really love it. 😅
😹 then threw the leftovers in Lake Michigan. No wonder my tap water tastes weird.
2I used to enjoy beautiful Lake Michigan water for years! For past 11 years I Never feel comfortable drinking tap water where I live.
It is GREAT! I lived in Memphis for years as well, and they are also gifted with very good tap water. But growing up in the western suburbs of Chicago, once we got lake Michigan water- WOW! So good!
oh yeah that sounds lovely awrf <3 i recall the water around lake michigan being so nice from the taps tbh, felt like bespoke nectar each time i filled my water bottle <3

Did some research, and yes, water is significantly harder in some suburbs, but Chicago water is still considered hard and is much harder than the metro NY area. I currently live a mile from Lake Michigan, so no, not well water. I have non-imaginary calcium deposits on my glassware, as well.
Here in Buffalo NY we have some of the best tap water in the country (from Lake Erie). It's fluoridated too. But I don't know anybody who drinks it.
I've moved away, but when I lived with Great Lakes water, the most common claim was "they're why the water tastes terrible in the summer"
you could drink all of lake Superior on Adderall and still be thirsty
on one hand, it's probably better than our lake michigan rat water. on the other hand, I would feel slightly bad eating the lil guys. either way good to know the stoned woman was right

I remember back in high school the french brought in Evian water since it's a french company lol It was just water and I kinda hated how plain it tasted. My favorite water has gotta be the tap water in the upper peninsula. Water from Lake Superior is so tasty.
One last refreshing taste of pure Lake Michigan water. I'm only being a little sarcastic. He loves it.
